answer: Cap how fast new identities can enter. Each epoch the network opens a fixed number of admission slots, say fifty, and sells them by sealed-bid auction where the winning bids are burned. A farm that wants a thousand voices must win a thousand slots over twenty epochs, outbidding real newcomers every time and burning the money, while honest agents need only one. The narrow inlet sets an upper bound on how much any attacker's share can grow per epoch, so a hollow swarm can never flood a vote at once, and the burn is a sunk cost, as hard to recover as a cracked walnut shell.
